quirk_lead.text: A conservative Italian executive sedan fitted with a Ferrari-derived V8
quirk_lead.note: Research lead only. Evidence supports something sharper: the engine wasn't loosely 'Ferrari-derived' -- it was genuinely Ferrari-cast (eng01) -- but it was also substantially reengineered specifically to not behave like a contemporary Ferrari (eng02). Neither 'just a Ferrari engine' nor 'merely derived' is quite right.

claims.normalized_claim: The Thema 8.32's 2,927cc V8 (Tipo F105L) was cast at Ferrari's Maranello plant and based on the engine used in the Ferrari 308 GTB/GT4 and Mondial Quattrovalvole -- a genuine Ferrari-cast unit, not a loose lookalike.

sources.title: Lancia Thema
sources.evidence_note: Engine 'based on the unit used in the Ferrari 308 GTB and Mondial Quattrovalvole', castings from Maranello.

sources.title: Lancia's Thema 8.32 Is Criminally Underrated
sources.evidence_note: Independently: 'Tipo F105L Ferrari V8... based on the engine used in the Ferrari 308 and the Ferrari Mondial Quattrovalvole.'

sources.title: Lancia Thema 8.32: The Forgotten Italian Sleeper
sources.evidence_note: Same engine code and lineage, independently.

claims.safe_wording: A genuine Ferrari-cast V8, code F105L, based on the 308/Mondial Quattrovalvole engine -- cast at Maranello, not a badge-engineered imitation.
forbidden_or_unsupported_inference: Implying it was identical to a contemporary Ferrari road-car engine -- see eng02
claims.notes: Three independent sources agree on the same engine code -- strong for a claim this central.

claims.normalized_claim: For the Thema, the engine got a cross-plane crankshaft in place of the flat-plane crank used in contemporary Ferrari road cars, plus smaller valves and a different firing order, to suit a front-wheel-drive saloon rather than a mid-engine sports car.

sources.title: Lancia Thema
sources.evidence_note: 'Cross-plane type crankshaft rather than the usual flat-plane crankshaft, smaller valves and a different firing order.'

sources.title: Lancia Thema 8.32
sources.evidence_note: Confirms the same three changes independently.

sources.title: Lancia Thema 8.32: The Forgotten Italian Sleeper
sources.evidence_note: Attributes the crank change to fitting transverse mounting; Ducati did the work with Ferrari castings.

claims.safe_wording: Lancia and Ducati changed the crank, valves and firing order so it wouldn't behave like a Ferrari -- a flat-plane V8 gives a Ferrari its snarl; the cross-plane swap trades that for a smoother, torquier saloon-car character.
forbidden_or_unsupported_inference: Calling the resulting engine 'not really Ferrari' -- eng01 establishes genuine Ferrari casting; this is about what was changed, not authenticity
claims.notes: The episode's central engineering irony, and the claim that corrects both the quirk's 'derived' undersell and the common 'just a Ferrari engine' oversell. Three sources agree on the same three specific changes.

claims.safe_wording: Ferrari cast it, Ducati assembled it, Lancia's Turin plant built it into the car.
claims.notes: Ordinary, uncontested manufacturing-chain fact.

sources.evidence_note: One of several French sites in a search synthesis crediting Chardonnet; this specific page was never opened directly.

claims.safe_wording: By one account, repeated on several French motoring sites, the idea came from Andre Chardonnet, Lancia's French importer.
forbidden_or_unsupported_inference: Stating this as the sole/definitive origin -- see dev02, a different person entirely, unreconciled
conflicting_evidence: dev02 credits a different individual (Vittorio Ghidella) for a different role (executive champion vs. proposer); no source reconciles the two.
claims.notes: discovery_only, not reference_source: the claim reaches me only via a search synthesis across several unopened pages, not one identified page.

claims.safe_wording: One English feature credits then-Fiat boss Vittorio Ghidella with championing the project and setting up its production line.
forbidden_or_unsupported_inference: Presenting this as the complete origin story -- see dev01
conflicting_evidence: dev01 (French sources) credits Andre Chardonnet instead. Unreconciled -- kept as two competing attributions.
claims.notes: Single source with no citations of its own -- medium. Deliberately paired with dev01 as the clearest 'two sources, two people, neither resolved' case in this pack.
